clue.text: Parental fuss is fatherly

indicators.note: a fuss is a commotion, so the letters get thrown into disorder and rearranged

parts.note: the word itself is the fodder

explanation.surface: A parent making a fuss over a child is being fatherly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parental' looks like part of the definition, but its eight letters are the fodder, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Paternal describes qualities or feelings typical of a father toward his children.

clue.text: Lied about being workshy

indicators.note: about can mean around or astray, so the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone told lies about how lazy they were.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means lazy or avoiding effort, which is what a workshy person is.

clue.text: King Charles consumes one by way of a delicacy

indicators.note: to consume is to take inside, so the royal letters swallow the other pieces

parts.note: Carolus Rex, the Latin royal cipher for King Charles
one and a are interchangeable
via is Latin for by way of

explanation.surface: A king tucks into something luxurious at a banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: The C and R of King Charles's cipher go around A and VIA to give CAVIAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviar, salted sturgeon roe, is a classic expensive luxury food.

clue.text: A jumping captain?

definitions.note: read as 'a jumping one', a person who skips
definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who skips, hops along
second meaning: the master of a boat or leader of a team

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a leaping ship's master; the question mark flags that one word carries both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is an informal name for the master of a boat or team, and literally one who skips or hops.

clue.text: A brother, as I've noted, can be harsh

parts.note: taken as written
BR is the standard abbreviation for brother
taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that their brother can have a rough manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive describes a rough, grating manner, so it is a synonym for harsh.

clue.text: Miser gets cut-price fish

parts.note: cut-price goods are cheap
a skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A stingy person buys fish at a discount.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is an informal word for a stingy person who hates spending money.

clue.text: Stalker reportedly makes suits

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining a noun: one who makes suits

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than seen, so we go by the sound of the word

parts.note: a stalker is one who tails someone, a tailer

explanation.surface: A stalker is said to make suits on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Tailer, one who tails, sounds like the maker of suits. The grid gives the surname spelling TAYLOR; the definition really wants TAILOR, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor is a craftsman whose trade is cutting and sewing made-to-measure garments such as suits.

clue.text: Country emblem provides recognisable feature on journey

parts.note: a land is a country
a mark is an emblem or sign

explanation.surface: A nation's symbol helps travellers know where they are.
explanation.definitionFit: A landmark is a prominent object that travellers use to orient themselves along a route.

clue.text: Decapitate Englishman immersed in evil

indicators.note: something immersed is plunged inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: bad means evil
E is the abbreviation for English, and HE stands for a man

explanation.surface: A wicked execution of an Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: To behead someone is to cut off their head, exactly what decapitating means.

clue.text: Hope Leeds United includes Brazilian star player

indicators.note: the words include, that is contain, the answer within their run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Leeds United fans hope to sign a Brazilian football legend.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds United is an English football club; the answer runs across the end of Hope and the start of Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelé was the Brazilian forward widely seen as the greatest footballer of all time.

clue.text: I can turn clamp inside, however unyielding

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece goes within the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to turn something is to twist it into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: fodder to be rearranged
if you can, you are able

explanation.surface: However firmly a clamp is fixed, someone insists they can turn it.
explanation.walkthrough: I and ABLE (for can) are split apart to take the rearranged letters between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Implacable means unable to be appeased or moved, so relentless and unyielding.

clue.text: It's not just an international carnival!

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, is an international body
a fair is a carnival

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a global festival is more than it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not just' reads as 'not merely', but here just means fair, so not just is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair means lacking justice or equity, so it is the opposite of just.

clue.text: Co-conspirator's account to police all about head of MI5

parts.note: ACC is a standard abbreviation for account

indicators.note: all about suggests things scattered every which way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the security service's name

explanation.surface: A plotter's financial records are handed to the police by the head of MI5.
explanation.walkthrough: MI5 is Britain's domestic security service.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice is a partner in wrongdoing, which is what a co-conspirator is.

clue.text: Ambassador takes oriental girl on a railway

parts.note: E for east, so oriental
a miss is a girl
taken as written
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A diplomat accompanies a young woman from the East on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is an envoy sent on a mission, much like an ambassador representing a state.

clue.text: Sugar makes sticky coating for lettuce

indicators.note: a coating surrounds what it covers, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: glue is sticky stuff
cos is a variety of lettuce

explanation.surface: Sugar can be used as a sticky glaze on salad leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Cos lettuce is the long-leaved kind Americans call romaine.
explanation.definitionFit: Glucose is a simple sugar, the main one carried in the blood.

clue.text: Blow money on North Dakota square dance

indicators.note: dancing moves things around, so the letters swap places

parts.note: ND is the postal abbreviation for North Dakota
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone wastes cash on a square dance in the American Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square dance' reads as one thing, but square is fodder and dance is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To squander is to waste money recklessly, which is what blowing money means informally.

clue.text: Returning paler, she loses heart to fall ill again

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, to be turned around

indicators.note: losing the heart means the middle letters go, leaving only the outside ones

parts.note: the word with its middle letter dropped

explanation.surface: A patient comes back looking pale and dispirited, sickening once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to deteriorate after a recovery, sliding back into sickness.

clue.text: Lacking the energy of a bullet?

definitions.note: a whimsical second sense: slug-ish, like a slug
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a slug is a bullet, so slug-ish means bullet-like

explanation.walkthrough: A slug is slang for a bullet, and the -ish ending means 'like', so the question mark flags a made-up sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggish means slow-moving and lethargic, short of vigour, as if one had no energy.

clue.text: Beat favourite dog

parts.note: to whip is to beat
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Someone thrashes their favourite hound.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippet is a breed of slim, fast racing dog similar to a small greyhound.

clue.text: Hot, lumpy stew from the home of the Brethren

indicators.note: a stew is a mixture of ingredients cooked together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: both words taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A steaming, lumpy casserole served by a religious community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' looks like the noun being described, but it signals the shuffle. The Plymouth Brethren are a Christian movement founded in that Devon port city.
explanation.definitionFit: The evangelical Christian movement known as the Plymouth Brethren took its name from the English city where it began.

clue.text: Set free two eggs seen in distorted lens

indicators.note: seen in places one piece within the other
something distorted is twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written
an egg looks like O, so two eggs are two Os

explanation.surface: A pair of eggs viewed through a warped lens appear to break loose.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen something is to release or untie it, letting it go free.

clue.text: Angel fish swallows queen

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a chub is a freshwater fish
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: An angelfish gulps down a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angel fish' reads as one creature; Angel is the definition and fish begins the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a kind of angel, often pictured as a winged child.

clue.text: Bird from the islands?

parts.note: surface reading: any tropical island bird; setter's reading: a small yellow songbird named after the Atlantic archipelago it comes from

explanation.walkthrough: The wild songbird is native to the Canary Islands, off north-west Africa, and is named after them.
explanation.definitionFit: The domestic songbird is descended from wild finches of the Atlantic archipelago and shares its name.

clue.text: Baker's tool places mixed grill on leg

indicators.note: mixed means jumbled together, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: both words taken as written, as fodder
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A baker puts a mixed grill on someone's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed grill' is a familiar dish, but mixed is the signal and grill on is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolling pin is the cylinder a baker uses to flatten out dough and pastry.

clue.text: Green but nevertheless wise!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a greyish-green colour, and the herb itself

explanation.surface: Someone inexperienced who is nonetheless shrewd.
explanation.walkthrough: Green suggests naive, the opposite of wise, which makes the clue sound contradictory.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a soft grey-green shade and an adjective for someone of profound judgment.

clue.text: Satire on society apparatus

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society
kit is equipment or apparatus

explanation.surface: A satirical piece mocks society's machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch that parodies or mocks its subject.

clue.text: Rest, losing time, get signal to save

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
a cue is a signal to act

explanation.surface: An actor rests until given the cue to come to someone's aid.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to save them from danger or harm.

clue.text: Very first listener to false story on saint

parts.note: the ear is what listens
a lie is a false story
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: The first person to hear a fabricated tale about a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliest is the superlative of early, meaning first in time of all.
